best_for: Photographers who shoot raw and want a free, open-source alternative to Lightroom for culling and developing, and who don't mind learning a different way of working.
description:
darktable is a free raw photo editor and photo library made by the darktable team, a group of developers who are photographers themselves. It is released under the GNU GPL version 3 or later.

Edits are built up as a stack of modules, from simple ones like crop, exposure and spot removal to a simulation of how the eye sees at night. The math runs in floating point, so it also handles scientific images and high dynamic range output from 3D renderers. Color management carries your colors through to print, and your graphics card can take on the processing to speed up work on the thousands of frames a long shoot can bring home.

points.title: Library plus raw developer
points.text: A lighttable view manages your photos in a database, and a darkroom view develops them. Raw files are decoded with rawspeed, and JPEG and HDR files open too.

points.title: Your originals stay untouched
points.text: Edits are stored as instructions and only applied when you export, so the original file is never changed and you can go back at any time.

points.title: Tethered shooting
points.text: darktable can control a connected camera and pull shots straight in, which few free tools do. Useful for studio and product work.

points.title: Apple silicon only on Mac
points.text: The official Mac build is for Apple silicon and needs macOS 14 or later. The project says there are no official releases for Intel Macs. The install page walks you through Gatekeeper warnings on first launch, and the Homebrew cask is disabled for failing Apple's check.

points.title: The Flatpak is a community build
points.text: Flathub marks the Linux Flatpak as unverified and not supported by the darktable developers, and the project notes it leaves out darktable's AI features. The project's own Linux builds are AppImages for x86_64 and aarch64.

points.title: Windows has both scopes
points.text: The Windows installer here is x64, for one user or all users. The project also offers a Windows on Arm build. The Windows listing keeps 36 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
